review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the definitions of lerayProjectionL2, stokesL2Operator, realLerayProjection and realStokesOperator in FourierLeray.lean and FourierRealification.lean. The Schwartz and Fourier lemmas (gradientOfCovector, weakTestGradientSchwartz_apply and _fourier, the Plancherel pairing lemma) are each used once, so they are not repeated machinery. The only repetition I found is in the two Leray/Stokes theorem pairs at the end of the file. It is a modest amount of reasoning (about 10 lines per copy), so the finding is of limited strength. I did not check that the proposed helpers compile.

findings.problem: The two *Representative theorems repeat the same argument. Each one applies realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal. Each one then rewrites ℱ(ℱ.symm (multiplier …)) back to the multiplier with apply_symm_apply. Each one turns the equality in Lp into an a.e. equality with Lp.ext_iff. Finally each runs filter_upwards [htransformAE, <multiplier>_divergence_free_ae …] and closes with rw [hξ]; exact hrange. The two wrapper theorems (realLerayProjection_isWeakDivFree and realStokesOperator_isWeakDivFree) repeat a second argument. Both set z, obtain hRange and hAE := realPartVectorL2Representative_eq_ae z, change the goal to the realPartVectorL2 form, and apply isWeakDivFree_congr_ae hAE.symm hRange. Only the operator differs.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two helpers before the concrete theorems.

(1) `theorem realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourier_eq_ae (v w : ComplexVectorL2) (hvw : MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ L2Vec3 ComplexVec3 v = w) (hw : ∀ᵐ ξ ∂volume, inner ℂ (complexifyFrequency ξ) (w ξ) = 0) : CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 (realPartVectorL2Representative v)`.
Proof sketch: `apply realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal; filter_upwards [(Lp.ext_iff).mp hvw, hw] with ξ h1 h2; rw [h1]; exact h2`.

(2) `theorem realPartVectorL2_isWeakDivFree_of_representative (z : ComplexVectorL2) (h : CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 (realPartVectorL2Representative z)) : CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2 (realVectorL2Representative (realPartVectorL2 z))`.
Proof sketch: `exact isWeakDivFree_congr_ae (realPartVectorL2Representative_eq_ae z).symm h`.

The Leray use is then `realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourier_eq_ae _ (lerayFourierMultiplier (ℱ (complexifyVectorL2 f))) (ℱ.apply_symm_apply _) (lerayFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae _)`. Here ℱ.apply_symm_apply _ is the existing `change ℱ (ℱ.symm …) = _` step. It should unify because lerayProjectionL2 unfolds to ℱ.symm (lerayFourierMultiplier (ℱ v)). The Stokes use has the same shape with stokesFourierMultiplier ht (ℱT …), ℱV.apply_symm_apply _ and stokesFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae ht _. The two non-Representative theorems become `realPartVectorL2_isWeakDivFree_of_representative _ (realLerayProjectionRepresentative_isWeakDivFree f)` and the Stokes analogue.
findings.benefit: Each concrete theorem shrinks from about 12 lines to a one- or two-line application. A future multiplier with divergence-free range (another Fourier multiplier operator) can reuse the helpers instead of copying the htransform / Lp.ext_iff / filter_upwards pattern. The argument that a Fourier multiplier with orthogonal range gives a weakly divergence-free real part is stated once.
